doc.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Favorite Basie players: Buck Clayton, Birdland nights and Joe Williams
summary: She names Lester Young and Buck Clayton, recalls Birdland in the 50s, and an ice cream talk with Joe Williams.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Who were some of your favorite characters, players, in the Basie groups over the years?

Well of course Lester was my Dream Prince of all time. Buck Clayton. I used to say to Harry Lim, “you like Buck Clayton?” “Yeah,” he says “I always remember John Hammond’s line was many times I have heard him but always muted.” So I thought he was married to Singsee, but it seems I think they were just live-in companions for a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

number of years. She was adorable. And she probably decided she wanted to get married and so she took off with Billy Kyle. I said to Harry Lim, “what do you think Buck Clayton said?” He said, “he probably took his mute out at that point.” I don’t know, I was just crazy about that band. Well there was a period in I guess it was in the 50s when they were playing at Birdland, and it was just like — well it was like going to church, I mean you just went regularly, you know you’d be marked absent if you weren’t there. I was very friendly with Dorothy Kilgallen, who was on my husband’s television show, “What’s My Line,” so we were a foursome. We used to go there regularly, many times every week just to check in all the time. And of course Joe Williams was our Dream Prince. And that man has the most marvelous total recall. I wish, as I’m getting on years, names are slipping away and dates and everything else. But he just, you can sit him down — I was walking along Central Park South one evening, and I ran into him. And he said, “I want to get some ice cream.” And I said, “we’re right at Rumpelmeyer’s, let’s go in, I’ll come with you, I’d like some.” We went and we sat there. We must have sat there for a couple of hours, over a sundae, an ice cream sundae. Because he was reminding me of all the places in Chicago in the south side, where everything was, who the owner was, who worked there, it was just so marvelous. And I’ve seen a video of a show like that in Los Angeles with Ernie Andrews. And he, but he’s in a car and he’s driving along and he says, “here’s where Black Dot McGee’s was” and here’s where something else was. But you could do that with Joe. It’d be heaven just to show everything about Chicago.
Now he got his start in Chicago, right?
And when you saw him with Basie, that was the time when he had the hit “Every Day?”
And “The Comeback” I loved you know. It was so marvelous. It was sensational, and he still sounds good. I love it when singers retain their vigor and their vocal qualities, it’s just so thrilling.
